correctness.rationale: All EF1 directional comparisons are explicitly reduced to a balanced vector and a real-H floor-dependent interval. Product maximization follows from the balancing exchange; log-concavity reduces worst EF1 to the endpoints. A complete two-case product comparison proves the dimension-dependent factor; an H-to-infinity family proves sharpness. Exact-fraction brute enumeration checked 228 finite instances with nonintegral H values included.

value.rationale: The exactly parameterized worst-EF1 objective quantifies the transition between the uniform-goods optimality regime and arbitrarily dominant exceptional items. A sharp factor for each n plus an explicit endpoint worst-outcome recipe are natural fairness-efficiency properties; neither a trivial restatement nor an arbitrary finite sample.
